**Unblocked — upstream #6259 closed, and the file face was re-verified on the merged ref before this card was returned to the queue.**

`Blocked-by: #6259` resolves: #6259 closed `completed` on 2026-08-25T13:06:16Z via merged PR #6305, *"drop the deprecated `width` from the drawer default, state the navConfig comment once"*.

The unlock scan re-measures the returning card's file face rather than trusting the card, because the merge that closed the upstream is the merge most likely to have swept the sibling sites too. **It did not.** Read from `main` through the contents API just now, and every line number in the card's table has moved, so the card's own table should be re-measured rather than trusted:

| file | card said | on `main` now | state |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | :--- |
| `packages/plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.tsx` | 1150 | **1285** | **converged** — `schema.navigation ?? { mode: 'drawer' }`, no width |
| `packages/plugin-gantt/src/ObjectGantt.tsx` (render site) | — | **1724** | **converged** — `width={navigation.width as any}`, no `??` literal |
| `packages/plugin-kanban/src/ObjectKanban.tsx` | 606 | **693** | unchanged — `?? { mode: 'drawer', width: 'min(960px, 60vw)' }` |
| `packages/plugin-kanban/src/ObjectKanban.tsx` | 899 | **995** | unchanged — `width={(navigation.width as any) ?? 'min(960px, 60vw)'}` |
| `packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx` | 389 | **449** | unchanged |
| `packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx` | 694 | **763** | unchanged |
| `packages/plugin-detail/src/RecordDetailDrawer.tsx` | 129 | **129** | unchanged — and this one is the *rationale home*, see below |

So the divergence this card predicted has actually happened: one of the three renderers moved, the other two did not.

## What the ruling decided, and what it explicitly did not

#6305 left its reasoning in the code (`ObjectGantt.tsx:1265-1284`), and it draws the boundary this card now sits on. Two separable halves, quoted from that comment:

**Decided — the `width` half, and it is zero-pixel:**

> No width is spelled here on purpose. `width` is `@deprecated [#2578 -> size]` in the spec that owns this shape, and `resolveOverlayWidth` gives an explicit `width` priority OVER `size` — so spelling it kept the deprecated branch load-bearing on the path most gantts take (no declared `navigation`), and made the size buckets unreachable there. Omitting both leaves `resolveOverlayWidth` returning `undefined`, which is what RecordDetailDrawer's own `width` default is for; that default is the identical `min(960px, 60vw)`, so this is a zero-pixel change on every viewport.

**Still open — the bucket half, and it is a real behaviour change:**

> Deliberately NOT converged on `size: 'lg'`: that bucket is `min(92vw, 960px)`, which agrees with the above only at viewport >= 1600px and is up to 53% wider below it. Whether the renderers should move to the bucket is open (#6259), and spans kanban/calendar/RecordDetailDrawer as one decision (#6303).

That second paragraph names this card by number as the home of the open decision. The card's own framing — *"the `width`/`size` question on #6259 decides all of them"* — turns out to be broader than what was actually decided: #6259 answered the `width` half for the gantt and deliberately left the bucket question open.

Returned to `pm:queue` on the decided half only. The dispatch will be scoped to it and will forbid the bucket move; the bucket question stays where the code comment puts it — on this card, for a human ruling — and nothing in the dispatched work may pre-empt it. Whether that warrants splitting the card in two is triage's call, not this seat's.

`RecordDetailDrawer.tsx:129` is deliberately excluded from the decided half: it is not a fourth copy of a default that should be deleted — it is the *source* of the default the other three now delegate to, and it carries the only written rationale for the value (`:76-78`). Deleting it is what would change pixels.

### Notes for the PM beyond the JSON

**Nothing in the dispatch order needed correcting.** Every line number matched, and the escalation clause did not fire — the measurement supports the zero-pixel ruling for kanban and calendar just as it did for the gantt.

**One check the order did not ask for, reported because its answer bears on whether this card is now fully discharged on the decided half:** a repo-wide sweep for a *fifth* divergent renderer found none. All three `navConfig` defaults now read `{ mode: 'drawer' }`; `plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` (`:1901`, `:1958`) already passes `navigationConfig?.width` with no literal fallback, so it delegates to the drawer too; `plugin-tree` and `plugin-map` use `useNavigationOverlay` but spell no width. After this PR the only remaining producer of `min(960px, 60vw)` in the repo is `RecordDetailDrawer.tsx:129` — the intended single source — plus comment text and the three pin tests' `EXPECTED_WIDTH` constants. No new issues filed.

**The open half is untouched and stays yours.** No renderer was moved to `size: 'lg'`, and `RecordDetailDrawer.tsx` was not edited. Leg B of the reverse-verification did *temporarily* mutate that file to prove half 2 is load-bearing; it was restored and the restoration proved by blob-hash identity (`da15724a89fbb2a8eb664c97f73f913281c9f6ce`), so it is byte-for-byte absent from the PR.

**CI status is `in_progress`** — reporting at draft-PR time per the dispatch contract; CI convergence is the PM's read, not mine.

**Post-merge verification — PR #6581 merged 2026-08-26T14:50Z. Measured on `main`: the dispatched half is clean, and the deferred half needs a new home (#6584).**

## The fix — the three renderers agree again

Read back from `main`. All three now have byte-equivalent shapes at both sites:

```
ObjectKanban.tsx:713    const navConfig = (schema as any).navigation ?? { mode: 'drawer' };
ObjectCalendar.tsx:466  const navConfig = (schema as any).navigation ?? { mode: 'drawer' };
ObjectGantt.tsx:1285    const navConfig = schema.navigation ?? { mode: 'drawer' };

ObjectKanban.tsx:1018   width={navigation.width as any}
ObjectCalendar.tsx:783  width={navigation.width as any}
ObjectGantt.tsx:1724    width={navigation.width as any}
```

**The literal now occurs in code exactly once** across the four files involved — `RecordDetailDrawer.tsx:129`, which is its home and the value the other three delegate to. Every remaining occurrence in the renderers is prose inside the explanatory comments (kanban 2, calendar 2, gantt 1, all non-code). That is the invariant this card existed to restore, and it holds.

## Both ⛔ exclusions survived

- **`RecordDetailDrawer.tsx:129` untouched** — `width = 'min(960px, 60vw)',` still there. Deleting it is what would have changed pixels, and it was excluded by name in the dispatch.
- **No move to `size: 'lg'`.** It appears exactly once per renderer, and every one of the three is the *"Deliberately NOT converged on `size: 'lg'`"* comment. Better than compliance: the deliberate non-action is now documented at all three sites rather than only at the one where it was first decided.

## ⚠️ The deferred half lost its tracker — filed as #6584

Those same three comments name the card that owns the open bucket decision, and post-merge that name is stale in every direction:

| file:line | names | state now |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ObjectKanban.tsx:712` | #6303 | **closed** (this card, by this merge) |
| `ObjectCalendar.tsx:465` | #6303 | **closed** |
| `ObjectGantt.tsx:1283` | #6259 and #6303 | **both closed** |

Nothing is broken in the shipped code; what is missing is a live home for a real published-behaviour question — `size: 'lg'` is `min(92vw, 960px)`, up to 53% wider below a 1600px viewport, across four record surfaces, and it has to be answered once for all four or the divergence this card closed re-opens.

Neither PR did anything wrong. #6305 answered the `width` half and pointed forward at this card; #6581 did the same for the other two renderers; `Fixes #6303` then closed the card and took the undecided half with it. **The reusable lesson, recorded on #6584: when a dispatch deliberately narrows to the decided half of a question, the open half needs its own card at dispatch time, not at merge time — and the code comments should point at that card from the start.** That is on this seat, which wrote the narrowing.

#6584 is filed unassigned and ungraded for triage.
